descriptionChirho: Qal active participle used as agent noun: one who murders or kills unlawfully, the manslayer/murderer, frequently in legal contexts of cities of refuge.
Qal finite verb forms meaning to murder or kill unlawfully, covering all persons, numbers, and tenses of the basic active stem.
Qal infinitive absolute used as a verbal noun denoting the act of murdering, often in lists of crimes.
Nifal stem expressing the passive: to be murdered or killed, including participial form for the one who has been slain.
Piel participle used as intensive agent noun: a habitual or deliberate murderer, one who murders as a characterizing activity.
Piel finite verb forms expressing intensive or repeated murder, denoting habitual or wholesale killing.
Pual (intensive passive) form expressing being murdered or slaughtered, the passive counterpart of the Piel.
